rows.access_level: ABSTRACT_ONLY (Europe PMC lists the article as subscription required, not in PMC; jaad.org PDF page returned HTTP 403, 2026-11-28)
rows.design: not in abstract [prevalence survey of 400 consecutive dermatology patients, a case-control study of fifteen IGH patients and fifteen matched controls, and uncontrolled treatment experiments within IGH lesions; whether the treated lesions came from the fifteen patients not in abstract]
rows.body_site: not in abstract [treated sites not stated; the abstract describes IGH macules in general as mainly affecting the exposed upper and lower extremities]
rows.skin_tone: not in abstract [controls were matched by skin type; the types are not stated]
rows.patients_enrolled: not in abstract [how many patients received this treatment not in abstract]
rows.analysis_unit: lesion [the abstract's statement is about lesions; no count given]
rows.comparator: not in abstract [no untreated or sham control arm described]
rows.citation: Falabella R, Escobar C, Giraldo N, Rovetto P, Gil J, Barona MI, Acosta F, Alzate A. On the pathogenesis of idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis. J Am Acad Dermatol 1987;16(1 Pt 1):35-44
rows.intervention: minigrafts of normal skin implanted in IGH lesions [autologous punch minigrafting; donor site, graft size and number not in abstract]
rows.endpoint_definition: change in the achromic defect after minigrafting (criteria not in abstract)
rows.arm_result: minigrafts did not modify the achromic defects; proportion of lesions, degree and timing not in abstract
rows.uncertainty: Abstract only; full text subscription only (paywall list). Number of patients, lesions and grafts treated, number of triamcinolone sessions, dose, follow-up length and assessment method are not in abstract, so no result can be timed from the final treatment and months after final treatment is NOT_DERIVABLE. The fifteen-patient group is described for the case-control work; whether the treated lesions belong to it not in abstract. 'Did not modify the achromic defects' and 'improved the appearance' give no proportion, degree or colour-match judgement, [so both rows are recorded as unquantified, not as partial repigmentation, complete area coverage or colour match]. The triamcinolone result is stated 'with or without grafts' as one group; the two subgroups are not separated in the abstract. Adverse effects (for intralesional steroid, e.g. atrophy) not in abstract. [Lead, not from this source: hirobe2018 (Discussion) cites Falabella et al. as reporting minigrafts in IGH becoming depigmented 18 months after grafting; that figure is not in this abstract and needs the full text.] [Module 5 leads, not ledger outcomes: the abstract reports patchy absence of melanocytes and melanin, epithelial atrophy, flattened rete pegs and basket weave hyperkeratosis; higher family prevalence of IGH in patients than controls; and no statistically established link with chronic sun exposure. Counts, tests and p-values for these are not in abstract.]

quotes.quote: Minigrafts of normal skin implanted in idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis lesions did not modify the achromic defects, whereas intralesional triamcinolone with or without grafts improved the appearance of these lesions.

In a group of 400 consecutive dermatologic patients, idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis was much more prevalent in women than in men.
In another group of fifteen patients with idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis and fifteen normal controls matched by age, sex, and skin type

small 2- to 5-mm achromic or hypopigmented macules, mainly affecting the exposed upper and lower extremities.
Epithelial atrophy, patchy absence of melanocytes and melanin, flattening of the rete pegs, and basket weave hyperkeratosis were the most prominent histologic findings
A family aggregation survey disclosed a higher prevalence of idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis in the family of patients with idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis than in the control group.
A cause-effect relationship between chronic actinic exposure and the development of idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis could not be established by statistical studies.
